ai.title: Fix supportsCacheControl model lookup
ai.summary: supportsCacheControl in common/src/constants.ts now uses Object.values(models) includes check instead of Record lookup. Previous generic cast allowed undefined key hits to bypass cache control guard. Unknown models default to false as before.

eli5.text: The assistant will no longer apply response caching to brand-new or unfamiliar models you ask it to use. Previously, the system checked whether a model was allowed to cache replies using a fast lookup table that could accidentally let any made-up model name slip through and wrongly enable caching; now it compares your model name against the explicit list of known models and simply skips caching when the name is not recognized. If you try to run a model that isn't in the official catalog today, you'll notice its responses aren't stored for faster reuse, matching the behavior of the earliest test builds.

ai.title: Fix type assertions in constants.ts
ai.summary: Replaced unsafe casts with `satisfies` constraints for `modelsGeneric` and `nonCacheableModels` in `common/src/constants.ts`. Removed redundant `satisfies` in `supportsCacheControl` argument check. Pure type-level refactor, no runtime behavior change.

eli5.text: The system's internal catalog of AI models had a spot where it guessed the shape of data using a blunt cast, which could hide real mistakes; it now uses a stricter check that still returns plain lists of model names but won't silently accept wrong types. This is purely behind-the-scenes housekeeping in the shared toolkit that powers many features, so no behavior you see changes today and nothing becomes faster, slower, or newly available. If you stared at the code, you'd notice two small swaps from unsafe casts to a `satisfies` constraint and a removed redundant assertion in a model lookup, but functionally the assistant still treats the same models the same way it did before.

ai.title: New USERINPUTPROMPT placeholder
ai.summary: Added USER_INPUT_PROMPT placeholder to templates. Uses parseUserMessage to extract raw text from <user_message> XML tags in history. Replaces ad-hoc JSON parsing in formatPrompt. Scope: backend templates and message utils.

eli5.text: The assistant now has a reliable way to pull your latest question out of the conversation history before building its reply, instead of relying on a rough text search that could misread curly braces or file paths in your message. This makes prompts that include your most recent input slightly more accurate, especially when your message contains characters or formatting that previously confused the old shortcut. The change is live now as part of the backend templates that shape every assistant turn.

ai.title: escapeString helper added to sanitize placeholder prompts
ai.summary: Added `escapeString` utility in `common/src/util/string.ts` to sanitize user input and initial agent prompts before template injection. Updated `backend/src/templates/strings.ts` to apply this escape to `PLACEHOLDER.USER_INPUT_PROMPT` and `PLACEHOLDER.INITIAL_AGENT_PROMPT`. Mechanism uses `JSON.stringify` and strips surrounding quotes to prevent prompt injection or template parsing errors from raw user strings.

eli5.text: When you type something into the assistant or set up a special starting instruction, the system now quietly cleans up those words behind the scenes before they get stitched into a longer prompt. This stops unusual characters or formatting in your input from accidentally breaking the prompt structure or trying to override instructions. You won't see anything different, but your messages and starter prompts are handled a bit more safely.

ai.title: Unified programmatic agent step handling
ai.summary: Refactors agent execution by removing ProgrammaticAgentTemplate and introducing a handleStep generator field on AgentTemplate. runProgrammaticAgent becomes runProgrammaticStep, managing generator state in-memory via agentIdToGenerator. This unifies LLM and programmatic agent paths in run-agent-step.ts, eliminating special-case branching for implementation types. Note: run-programmatic-step.ts contains a hardcoded throw new Error('Not implemented yet!') preventing programmatic agent execution.

eli5.text: The system that runs automated assistant tasks has been reorganized so that all agents go through the same single pathway, instead of having a separate, older route just for programmatic agents. If you watched the logs or configuration today, you would no longer see the term 'programmatic agent' as a distinct category; instead every agent is handled as a step in a unified flow. Behind the scenes, the short-term working memory for each agent is kept in the server's memory rather than passed around, which is an internal housekeeping change aimed at stability. Note: the evidence shows a placeholder that throws an error still exists, so this consolidation is in place but does not yet enable programmatic agent execution.

ai.title: Docs: remove override guide, add parentInstructions
ai.summary: Agent docs drop the override section and key terms, replacing it with from-scratch template guidance. New parentInstructions field added to examples and a dedicated section in creating-new-agents.mdx. Overview.mdx introduces Agent Coordination via parent instructions. Covers web/src/content/agents/ files.

eli5.text: The written guidance for building helper assistants has been rewritten: the section showing how to tweak an existing assistant is gone, replaced with step-by-step instructions for making one from scratch, and a new field lets an assistant give specific directions to the helper assistants it creates. If you read the docs today, you would no longer see the old override instructions and would instead find advice on defining each assistant entirely on its own, plus a new section showing exactly how to hand off guidance to sub-assistants. The change is live in the documentation now, affecting anyone reading the internal agent-building guides, but it only reorganizes and clarifies existing capabilities rather than adding new ones.
